attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post.

semantics.note: Present-tense claim that losses make OpenAI dependent on investors. The 'because X, so Y' structure is captured correctly. No horizon or condition is dropped.

contract.note: Taking calendar 2025 as the period and reading 'at the mercy' as reliance on outside capital is an ordinary plain reading. It does not stretch the claim for or against him.

evidence.note: Loss of about $11.5B for Q3 2025, worked out from Microsoft's equity-method filing. It is derived but falls inside the period.
Reported investor documents projected a 2025 net loss of about $9B. This is an estimate published before the period ended.
Fortune says the strategy needs near-constant fundraising, which backs the reliance-on-capital part.
FT-verified 2025 accounts show a large loss: about $8B even after removing one-time charges. Published before the evaluation date.
The CFO says OpenAI could break even if it wanted to. This is the company talking about itself, not a finding, so it does not show OpenAI was self-funding.

reviews.rationale: Several independent sources agree OpenAI ran large net losses in 2025: about $8–9B underlying and far more on a headline basis. Reporting also says it needed near-constant outside fundraising. The CFO's break-even remark is a company statement and shows no 2025 self-funding. The support condition is met.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post.

semantics.note: A firm 'will' with an explicit antecedent ('if things continue to deteriorate'), which is kept. No deadline was given.

contract.note: The antecedent has no measure or time frame, and 'a lot harder' has no threshold. The contract admits the result depends on these readings and treats the condition as unknown.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own growth figures. Being self-reported, they speak to the antecedent but do not independently show whether deterioration happened.
The next primary round was $110B at a $730B pre-money valuation. This matters only if the antecedent held.
The previous primary round, $40B at $300B post-money, for comparison.
Amazon's tranche was staged and conditional, a modest sign of tougher terms. The round still came in much larger.

reviews.rationale: This is a conditional forecast. The packet does not show whether OpenAI's position kept deteriorating after December 2025; the only signal is OpenAI's own self-reported growth. With the antecedent unknown, the claim is not scored, even though the next round was larger and at a higher valuation. No early-resolution event is met.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post.

semantics.note: 'Stand to take a sizable loss' describes exposure, a possibility rather than a firm outcome. It is also conditional on OpenAI losing its trajectory. The drafter recorded the modality as 'could'.

contract.note: The contract itself calls 'stand to' a hedge, yet sets support and contradiction conditions and a plain reading as if the claim were firm. Under policy, hedged language is not scored, so it holds him to more than he said.

evidence.note: OpenAI's post-money valuation rose to $852B in March 2026. This bears on the antecedent (it did not happen), not on any pension fund outcome.

reviews.rationale: 'Stand to take a sizable loss' is possibility language about exposure, so policy says it is not scored. Even read firmly, the antecedent had not happened by the evidence cutoff: OpenAI's valuation kept rising. No source confirms CalPERS's exposure either.
